Can you summarize the support ticket trends for XStream Pro and recommend next steps?

Support tickets for XStream Pro have climbed steadily this quarter, with escalations concentrated in the enterprise tier +2. The pattern points to reliability rather than usability — most reports cite unexpected disconnects during peak hours.

Sentiment across recent coverage echoes the same theme Yahoo News+2, with customers describing the service as “unpredictable.”

Supporting evidence

Escalation volume rose from 120 in May to 190 in July, and Level 2–3 cases now make up 30% of the total — a clear sign of increasing complexity.

“

XStream Pro has been unpredictable and disruptive. It’s affecting our ability to deliver consistent service to our clients.

Suggested next steps

  • Launch an escalation-prevention program focused on early detection.
  • Review staffing levels against sustained Level 2–3 complexity.
  • Invest in automation and cross-team collaboration.

Usage

How a response is built. A Response is a Turn that composes existing pieces — a user message, an optional Latency state, the Copilot message as a stack of Response Blocks (16px apart) with inline Citations, and the Response Footer. Templates are flexible blueprints that adapt to any context in Light and Dark.

Do

  • Compose the body from Response Blocks at the exact type scale, 16px apart.
  • Reuse the Citation pill inline (Work for enterprise sources, Web for open web).
  • Reuse the Response Footer for actions and the References avatar stack.
  • Right-align the user message in a subtle bubble; keep the reply full-width.

Don't

  • Re-typeset blocks — use the Segoe Sans / Georgia / Consolas scale as-is.
  • Rebuild the footer or citation — compose the existing components.
  • Mix content and functional type inside a reading block.
  • Crowd blocks together — preserve the 16px rhythm and the quote’s breathing room.
